headline: Regent Chairman Shahed arrested again in money laundering case
summary: A Dhaka court has ordered the arrest of Regent Hospital Chairman Mohammad Shahed Karim in a corruption case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission.
details: A Dhaka special judge's court has ordered the arrest of Regent Hospital Chairman Mohammad Shahed Karim. The order comes in a case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) regarding money laundering and the acquisition of assets beyond known sources of income.
The decision was made on Monday by Judge Mohammad Abdullah Al Mamun of the Special Judge's Court-5, following a hearing on an application by the ACC.
Shahed's lawyer, Dabir Uddin, stated that a bail application was filed today, but it was not heard. The hearing for the bail application and the framing of charges will take place on September 27.
Shahed's wife, Sadia Arabi, is currently on bail, having been granted bail on September 1. The ACC filed the case on March 7, 2021, and submitted the charge sheet on January 10, 2024.
Mohammad Shahed Karim has previously been in the center of controversy for alleged fraud regarding sample testing during the COVID-19 pandemic. He currently faces over 35 cases.
caption:
Regent Hospital Chairman Shahed is back in custody. A court has ordered his arrest in a money laundering case.

A Dhaka special judge's court has ordered the arrest of Regent Hospital Chairman Mohammad Shahed Karim. The order comes in a case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) regarding money laundering and the acquisition of assets beyond known sources of income.

The decision was made on Monday by Judge Mohammad Abdullah Al Mamun of the Special Judge's Court-5, following a hearing on an application by the ACC.

Shahed's lawyer, Dabir Uddin, stated that a bail application was filed today, but it was not heard. The hearing for the bail application and the framing of charges will take place on September 27.

Shahed's wife, Sadia Arabi, is currently on bail, having been granted bail on September 1. The ACC filed the case on March 7, 2021, and submitted the charge sheet on January 10, 2024.

Mohammad Shahed Karim has previously been in the center of controversy for alleged fraud regarding sample testing during the COVID-19 pandemic. He currently faces over 35 cases.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo

headline: Dozens injured as sacked Islami Bank employees and consumer forum clash in Dhaka
summary: Violence erupted in front of the bank's head office as sacked employees demanding reinstatement clashed with members of the Sachetan Grahak Forum.
details: Dozens of people were injured today after sacked employees of Islami Bank Bangladesh and members of the Sachetan Grahak Forum clashed in front of the bank's head office in Dhaka.
The sacked employees, who were recruited during the S Alam Group's tenure, had gathered outside the bank for the second consecutive day to demand their reinstatement.
Simultaneously, members of the consumer forum staged a demonstration at the same site, leading to a confrontation where both groups chased and attacked each other.
Shahidul Islam, one of the sacked employees, claimed that 25 of their members were injured in the attack and were admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Nuru-Un-Nabi Manik, president of the Sachetan Grahak Forum, countered this by claiming around 30 of its members were injured, including five seriously.
Manik alleged that the sacked employees, whom he described as illegally recruited, were attempting to create instability at the bank and that the attack was carried out under police protection.
Police eventually intervened and removed the protesters from the spot to restore order.
The officer-in-charge of Motijheel Police Station could not be reached for comment regarding the incident.
caption:
Dozens injured in Dhaka as sacked Islami Bank employees and a consumer forum clash over reinstatement demands.

Dozens of people were injured today after sacked employees of Islami Bank Bangladesh and members of the Sachetan Grahak Forum clashed in front of the bank's head office in Dhaka.

The sacked employees, who were recruited during the S Alam Group's tenure, had gathered outside the bank for the second consecutive day to demand their reinstatement.

Simultaneously, members of the consumer forum staged a demonstration at the same site, leading to a confrontation where both groups chased and attacked each other.

Shahidul Islam, one of the sacked employees, claimed that 25 of their members were injured in the attack and were admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Nuru-Un-Nabi Manik, president of the Sachetan Grahak Forum, countered this by claiming around 30 of its members were injured, including five seriously.

Manik alleged that the sacked employees, whom he described as illegally recruited, were attempting to create instability at the bank and that the attack was carried out under police protection.

Police eventually intervened and removed the protesters from the spot to restore order.

The officer-in-charge of Motijheel Police Station could not be reached for comment regarding the incident.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #IslamiBank #Protest #News

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
